product: VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0 — vSphere Automation API for vCenter

derived_from.note: Pinned to the 9.0.0.0 revision of this file. The 9.1.0.0 revision of the same path is a different contract; see forbidden_body_properties.

envelope: none — the /api surface returns the payload directly; there is no {"value": ...} wrapper (that belonged to the deprecated /rest surface)

idempotency.spec_text: Client-generated token used to retry a request if the client fails to get a response from the server. If the original request succeeded, the result of that request will be returned, otherwise the operation will be retried. If missing or `null`, the server will create a token.
idempotency.format: UUID — lowercase 8-4-4-4 hex groups then 12 hex digits; a token that does not conform to the UUID format is rejected with 400 InvalidArgument
idempotency.rule: one logical deploy uses exactly one token; every retry of that deploy re-sends the identical token so the server replays the original result instead of deploying twice

request_body.omission_rule: Every optional property documents 'If missing or `null`, the server will ...'. An unset optional property is OMITTED from the JSON object. It is never sent as "", as an empty object, as an empty array, or as null. accept_all_eula is required, so it is sent even when its value is false.
request_body.naming: body properties are snake_case; the path parameter (ovfLibraryItemId) and the header (Client-Token) are not

error.errors_item: Vcenter.Ovf.OvfError — required category (VALIDATION|INPUT|SERVER), optional message (Vapi.Std.LocalizableMessage with required id, default_message, args)

200.note: succeeded=false is a completed-and-failed deploy reported with HTTP 200. It is a final answer, not a transient condition.

responses.503: Vapi.Std.Errors.ServiceUnavailable — 'If the service is not available.'

query.names: uniqueItems array of string, style: form, explode: true — several names are sent as repeated names=<value> pairs; omitted entirely when no filter is applied

retry_policy.rationale: The Client-Token header exists so that a deploy the client did not see the answer to can be re-sent safely. Retrying is therefore correct exactly where the outcome is unknown or the server declared itself unavailable.
retryable: transport failure — the request was sent but no complete HTTP response came back (connection reset, EOF, response truncated)
not_retryable: HTTP 400 / 403 / 404 — the request itself is wrong; re-sending it changes nothing
HTTP 200 with succeeded=false — the deploy ran and failed; it is a final result
retry_policy.sleep: through an injected sleep function so tests never wait on a real clock

forbidden_body_properties.subnet_mappings: added to Vcenter.Ovf.LibraryItem.ResourcePoolDeploymentSpec in the 9.1.0.0 revision of this file; absent from 9.0.0.0
forbidden_body_properties.tag_params: added to Vcenter.Ovf.LibraryItem.ResourcePoolDeploymentSpec in the 9.1.0.0 revision of this file; absent from 9.0.0.0
forbidden_body_properties.client_token: the idempotency token travels in the Client-Token header, never in the request body
forbidden_body_properties.camelCase_spellings: resourcePoolId, hostId, folderId, acceptAllEula, deploymentSpec, networkMappings, storageProvisioning, storageProfileId, defaultDatastoreId — the body is snake_case

not_this_operation.Vcenter.Ovfs_deploy$Task: path key /vcenter/ovfs?action=deploy&vmw-task=true, added in vSphere API 9.0.0.0. A task-based deploy from a web-served OVF URL. It declares no Client-Token header, so it is not the retry-safe library-item deploy this contract pins.
